newsitem.title: UK: ACPC plans technical talks to review coffee market.
newsitem.headline: ACPC plans technical talks to review coffee market.

text.p: The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) has called a meeting of its technical group in May to analyse the surge in coffee prices and its effect on consumption, secretary general Roberio Oliveira Silva said.

The group, which consists of Brazil, Colombia, El Salvador, Indonesia, Ivory Coast and Uganda, will, if necessary, suggest measures to arrest the price hike and ensure a steady supply of coffee to the market.
"We don't want (high prices) to hit consumption levels," Silva told Reuters.
"We are very concerned about the likely factor that high prices can have on consumption," he said.
But Silva added that although producers were keen to reduce the tightness in the supply of arabica coffee, they were concerned about the large discount at which robusta coffee is trading to arabica.
"We still have plenty of room (for price increase) in the case of robusta," he said.
The technical group will report its findings and any necessary measures to the ACPC Council which will also be held in May.
But Silva said there was also the possibility of holding the Council meeting earlier than scheduled.
